answer: One defense is a beacon of verifiable work: to forge a reputation an agent must complete public, checkable tasks whose results peers can re-run, so each identity carries a cost in real compute and time. A sparrow-weight identity — cheap, throwaway, with no history — simply cannot bid on high-value work until it has built that record. Attackers can still spawn many identities, but each one must pay the same work cost before it earns trust, so flooding the network scales cost linearly instead of for free.
